legal_analysis: The President established the Committee in EO13038 section1 and prescribed a report-relative sunset in section4. Section2 requires the report to the Vice President. Actual December18 submission is independently supported; it is not inferred from the December31 reporting deadline or public release. Thirty calendar days later is January17. No filing-deadline weekend rule or precise clock time is asserted.

FACA section9(c)(I) requires the charter to state an early termination date. It does not independently grant the charter signer authority to change a Presidential order. The1998 CFR section101-6.1031(a) requires amendment of charter sections affected by a new Presidential order and filing of the amended charter. Its distinction from the broader agency-charter amendment provision in1031(b) matters: this Committee was already established by the President, not independently created under general Commerce authority.

Parent section3(e) delegates Presidential FACA functions and therefore has substantive administrative effect. The record does not establish that it empowers the delegate to contradict the specific establishment/sunset terms of that same Presidential order. The charter signer might have been a designee; his different title is not treated as proof of invalidity. Likewise, the reservation of Presidential extension in section4 does not by itself prohibit every possible earlier termination.

The serious contrary reading treats the signed mandatory October31 charter clause as a competent delegated termination act. CFR101-6.1027 recognizes earlier termination by revoking or abolishing establishment authority and requires agency notice. A termination need not carry a particular document title. Even so, the reproduced charter pairs the old October1 reporting date with October31 duration and is expressly pursuant to the Presidential order. The later President-issued September25 deadline extension, preserved section4 formula and1031(a) conformity requirement support treating that paired schedule as superseded implementation language, rather than an independent contrary exercise of termination authority.

The conclusion does not depend on inferring a missing renewal or proving that every amended charter was filed. Initial filing, amended filing, continued legal establishment, and lawful committee operation are separate questions. Statutory two-year termination from March11 1997 had not yet occurred at either proposed date. The existence-without-action rule for committees directed by statute in1029(a)(1) is not applied to this Committee. If a competent earlier termination is proved,1029(b) and FACA14 renewal/charter requirements would be material; requiring them unconditionally would assume that disputed earlier ending.

The charter footnote discrepancy (June17 1997 for duration versus June17 1998 for reporting change) and later work are retained as context, not independently decisive authority. EO13138 sections3(b),9 later revokes the parent and named amendments effective September30 1999 and confirms prior completion/termination, without establishing the earliest date.

The charter-authority issue is now resolved in favor of the January17 legal reading on these sources. However, EO13138 identifies earlier amendments EO13062 section5 and EO13065, and the report describes amendments among other things. Their complete operative texts were not supplied or independently inspected in this exact version. A whole-chain assertion that no intervening term altered section3(e),section4 or another relevant independent command is therefore still unverified. This is a narrow evidence-completeness hold, not a repetition of the missing-charter theory or a procedural-approval hold.
